description:
FILED s463av, found while writing the #981 guard rows.  PRE-EXISTING — the code
involved is untouched by #981 (probed on the base tree as well).

    my @d = (1,2,3);
    delete $d[1];
    my @copy = @d;
    print scalar(@copy), " ", (exists $copy[1] ? "exists" : "hole"), "\n";

    perl 5.40.3 : 3 exists
    PCL         : 3 hole

The LENGTH and the VALUES agree (3 slots, element 1 undef, element 2 = 3) — the
divergence is `exists` alone.

WHY.  A hole is `nil` in an element slot: `exists` is false, a read gives undef,
the first write boxes it (this is the deleted-element marker, deliberately
distinct from undef-but-exists).  `%p-snapshot-array-rhs` copies nil through,
and `%p-array-fill-item`'s `((null item) (vector-push-extend nil target))` arm
stores it as a hole again — so the marker propagates across an assignment.

Perl does not work that way: `my @copy = @d` puts @d in LIST context, and
flattening an array to a list turns a hole into an ordinary undef.  The hole is
a property of the ARRAY, not of the values it yields; it cannot survive being
flattened and re-assembled.  (It does survive `\@d` / `$d[1]` / an alias — the
array itself is unchanged there.)

WHERE THE FIX GOES: `%p-array-fill-item`'s `(null item)` arm is reached from
p-array-fill's walk of an already-flattened source, so it cannot distinguish
"this array had a hole here" from "this list has an undef here" — it should
store undef.  But the SAME arm is what preserves holes for the paths that must
preserve them, so check which callers reach it before changing it: the
distinction is LIST-context flattening (holes die) versus a structural copy
(holes live).  `%p-snapshot-array-rhs` deliberately preserves nil for
`@a = (1, @a, 2)` to work at all, so the nil must survive the snapshot and die
at the store, not earlier.

SIZE: unknown; no baseline row is known to sit behind it.  Probe the sweep for
`exists` on a copied array before scheduling.
subject: A deleted array element's HOLE survives a whole-array copy in PCL; in perl the copy flattens to a list and the hole becomes an ordinary existing undef
